statement: On the tile ground that the played build shows, main's beam-clash clip reads 6.5 flashes a second with Reduce flashing on and 5.5 with it off, against a limit of 3, and no pixel reading exists for the played commit 6a30b4c9.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (CD-04 has been open since 2026-11-07 with three directors named)
risk: An outside tester without the owner's standing sees scenes over the limit even with Reduce flashing locked on; early sign is the first tiles=1 clip set read on the candidate.

statement: No desktop package for an outside tester can be made today: the build workflow needs a recorded approval file that does not exist, the package text step reads a notice file still marked draft, and the workflow has never run.
evidence: ci:gh run list --workflow desktop-builds.yml returned no runs (read 2026-11-13)
risk: A tester build made by hand outside the workflow would skip the lock, the route scan and the notices; early sign is any tester folder without README.txt and NOTICES.txt.
orb_question: When the gates are green, will you record one line saying yes to desktop test builds for named outside testers?

statement: The list of gates that must be green before an outside tester plays did not exist before this audit, and several of its gates have no saved record or no tool.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the list is drafted in LEGAL.md of this audit)
risk: Without one list a candidate is called ready on CI alone; early sign is a candidate commit with no docs/legal/runs/<sha>/ folder.

statement: No ruling or package covers an outside tester playing the LAN modes: the locked package refuses any network code, and the LAN folder's terms name only the owner and the trusted second player.
risk: A tester is handed the owner's LAN folder with terms that do not fit them and a firewall step they cannot judge; early sign is any plan that sends the LAN folder to a friend.
orb_question: In the first Alpha round, are the LAN modes for you and the trusted second player only, or for outside friends too?

statement: The tester note is a draft for the owner to send, its review row is still open on two conditions, and nothing records how a tester confirms being an adult or agrees to the terms.
risk: A tester plays without having read the safety and privacy words; early sign is a download key issued with no dated acknowledgement.

statement: Legal asked that report files be checked for account names and file paths before a tester sends them, and no such check exists; the LAN folder's report script points at the owner's own project folder and needs Node.
risk: A tester posts a file carrying their account name to a third-party service; early sign is a scan of the first real report folder.

statement: The report channel is undecided: the owner's words were to convert an existing server, Legal's first flag says not to, and no record settles the three items Legal wants settled before the first tester.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (an owner action plus one Legal read)
risk: Reports, builds or in-progress character art are seen by people who are not testers; early sign is an invite link that works for a non-tester.
orb_question: Will you use a new private server (or a new channel locked to a tester role) for reports, and keep the promise to delete a tester's reports on request?

statement: The repairs to the flash measuring chain ordered on 2026-11-07 (CD-09) have no commit: the analyser file is unchanged, no flash reading runs on a schedule, the last nightly is from 2026-10-30 on an old commit, and the recorded release pass is for a commit of 2026-10-15.
risk: A pass on the candidate would rest on an analyser with a known counting flaw; early sign is the self-test still passing on the old tie code.

statement: Whether a restricted, key-only itch.io page may go up before the title search is not confirmed anywhere: Legal's own page and the audit directive both say the search comes before any itch.io page, and the plan row is empty.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (one Legal row; a paid search is the owner's spend)
risk: The itch.io page is made under a title that later has to change; early sign is the page being created before a Legal row exists.
orb_question: May the private, key-only itch.io page go up under the working title before the paid title search, if Legal writes that it is unlisted and unpromoted?

statement: The owner's one-line licence choice is not on record, so the build says the licence is not chosen yet and no plain permission page exists.
risk: Testers and contributors do not know what they may do with the build; early sign is a tester asking whether clips may be shared.
orb_question: Do you agree to keep everything all rights reserved through Alpha, with a short friendly permission page, and decide about public code at Beta?

statement: Three older Legal pages still recommend the permissive pairing that the current rundown says never to use.
risk: A later session acts on the older page; early sign is a LICENSE draft reappearing at the root.

statement: The privacy words differ between the package README, the in-game About page and the tester note, and none of the words inside a build mention the two-PC link or the report channel.
risk: A build with the LAN modes carries a line saying it makes no network connection; early sign is the package check passing on a build that holds net code.

statement: In a desktop build the AI disclosure is not on the first screen: the start notice carries only the flashing words, and the AI line sits in README.txt and on the About page.
risk: A Steam Deck tester who starts the game from a shortcut never opens README.txt; early sign is the tester checklist's first-screen step.

statement: The content-rating records disagree with the game: the owner's early answer says graphic violence with a Mature target, bystanders now never die, a finisher marked graphic is still in the data, and the store-readiness list (CD-13) has not been rebuilt.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the list only; removing the finisher from data would be a separate hashed change)
risk: A store survey is answered from stale records at Beta; early sign is the Steam demo plan citing the old rating line.

statement: The public repository's safety net ordered on 2026-11-07 (CD-11: secret scanning, push protection, a protected main) has no commit or record, and its state today is not evidenced.
risk: A key or a tester's report is pushed to the public repository by mistake; early sign is the content screen being the only check on a push.

statement: The flashing-effects notice is the first thing in a session, has no timeout, is raised once per session with nothing remembered, and a locked build honours none of the words that skip it.
Reduce flashing is on by default, the packaging tools set the lock that hides its toggle, and the kept LAN build's own data shows the lock on.

By a read of the game's scripts, nothing sends data by itself: no web request class is used anywhere, the only network socket is the LAN link in net/, and the one hand-off to a browser is the feedback button, whose target is off by default and in both kept builds.

Bystanders never die in the sim: the one function that moves people removes, hurts and counts nobody, no kill function or casualty write remains, and two checks for it are on the world job's run list.

Credits and third-party notices are inside the game: the licences page takes the engine's own licence texts at run time, the About page names the engine and the font, and the package tool writes and checks a NOTICES.txt.

Legal's licence rundown is current and complete for the specification's question: three kinds of work, five options against itch.io, Steam, control and contributors, and one recommendation with reasons.

The tester note's words cover every X-32 item: the AI line up front, adults only, a private build, what a tester agrees to, the privacy line with the report channel named as a third party, and where the credits are.
The public test build is down and watched: the site switch is offline, and the daily watch job passed on each of the last three days.
The public-repository content screen and the workflow lint both passed on the baseline commit.
A saved LAN match file holds the build, the mode, timings and the replay, and by the code that writes it no account name, file path or network address.
